p01.why: Opens inside the most famous hand in poker with the money in and a villain on a draw, then asks the exact question every player has muttered at the river.

p27.why: Quotes the viewer's own complaint word for word and answers it in one flat line that contradicts it.

p37.why: A moment everyone has stood up for, the whole table waiting on one card, with the real number dropped while the tension is still on.

p33.why: Twelve words of a loss the viewer has lived, ending on the feeling the reel will test.

p12.why: A taggable type every regular knows, deflated with one number.

p08.why: Pure scene with a stake and the river still to come, so the viewer stays for the card.

p06.why: A sworn verdict on a recognisable type, backed by a number that stings.

p14.why: Puts the viewer's own cards on the table and names the certainty they feel before puncturing it.

p34.why: The fold you replay all week is a regret anyone recognises, and the line turns it into a way to judge it.

p39.why: Catches the viewer the morning after a good night, about to make the mistake the number warns against.
